title: Sulfur Metabolism in Yeast Strains
summary: This cluster revolves around the sulfur metabolism in yeast strains, particularly focusing on the genes and proteins involved in this process. The Met17 enzyme plays a crucial role in catalyzing the conversion of sulfate to homocysteine. The HSU1 gene has a pleiotropic role in sulfate metabolism and is involved in the expression of met17Δ. The met17Δ strain exhibits inefficient sulfide assimilation, while the hsu1Δ strain shows a consistent fitness defect under sulfur limitation. The accumulation of hydrogen sulfide is mediated by the met17 deletion in Sonal et al.'s study. The sulfate can grow on met17 mutants and is the source of both H2S and sulfide.
